findings.title: Offset restoration needed positive proof of an owned, uninterrupted cap suspension
findings.failure: Empty claims leave isCurrent() true; a same-claim write can change revision while remaining current. The earlier host finally could restore an old offset even when no owned cap was suspended or the transaction was interrupted.
findings.resolution: Require measurement.changed and measurement.restored plus current generation/ownership and an actual offset difference. The style helper preserves claim identity and revision; changed requires a field different from its authored baseline.
findings.evidence: Static review plus final public empty-claim/successor controls and same-claim, full/partial-handoff controls in the 351-pass run. No separate historical red execution is claimed for this finding.

findings.title: A throwing restoration setter could falsely certify a partially restored snapshot
findings.failure: With projected width/height300/400 and authored100/200, the width restoration setter wrote300 then threw. The old loop stopped with height200 yet completion.restored=true and isCurrent=true.
findings.resolution: Continue only while original ownership/revision/current guards remain valid, preserve the first error, and certify every final value and priority against the original projection snapshot.
findings.evidence: The reviewer directly executed the old helper counterexample and both repaired helper controls with actual Happy DOM style operations and an instrumented throwing setter; these are local ownership controls, not native-browser evidence.
